newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian spring sowing ahead of schedule - agency.
newsitem.headline: Russian spring sowing ahead of schedule - agency.

text.p: Russia's spring sowing is rolling ahead of schedule despite the usual shortage of fuel and lubricants, Interfax news agency said on Tuesday, quoting a senior Agriculture Ministry official.

Ivan Gridasov, head of the crops department, said the spring crop acreage by May 4 was 9.2 million hectares, 284,000 hectares more than a year earlier and 16 percent above the planned level, Interfax said.

According to Gridasov, sowing of grains crops was 505,000 hectares up compared with last year at 6.5 million hectares. Sowing of annual grass crops was up by 32,000 hectares at 982,000 hectares of sown land.

However, sowing of sunflower crops declined by 120,000 hectares compared with last year to 478,000 hectares, with sowing of corn crops falling by 40,000 hectares to 130,000. Sugarbeet planting was also down by 81,000 hectares at 368,000 hectares.

Gridasov said for this spring's sowing the farming sector received 570,000 tonnes of fertilisers, up 30,000 tonnes on last year. The acreage of fertilised land rose by 1 million hectares to 3 million hectares.

Interfax quoted Gridasov as saying fuel and lubricants supply for the farming sector was "still very tight". By April 24 farmers had received only 804,400 tonnes of diesel and 408,700 of petrol out of 6.5 million tonnes of diesel and 2.7 million tonnes of petrol due in the first half of 1997, he said. --Moscow Newsroom +7095 941-8520
